pitta-vriddhi.text: Observed Pitta vriddhi: dravyas recorded as Pitta-pacifying are marked as supporting; dravyas recorded as Pitta-aggravating or of Ushna virya are flagged for review (classical rationale, not an objective measurement).

kapha-vriddhi.text: Observed Kapha vriddhi: Kapha-pacifying dravyas marked as supporting; Kapha-aggravating dravyas flagged for review.

vata-vriddhi.text: Observed Vata vriddhi: Vata-pacifying dravyas marked as supporting; Vata-aggravating dravyas flagged for review.

manda.text: Manda agni recorded: formulations/herbs with recorded Deepana/Pachana or Agnimandya indications are marked as contextually relevant.

tikshna.text: Tikshna agni recorded: Ushna-virya dravyas flagged for review.

present.text: Ama recorded as present: the classical line of treatment emphasises Ama pachana and strengthening Agni first; formulations with recorded Ama-pachana/Deepana indications are marked as contextually relevant.

note.text: Rare cases of clinically apparent liver injury (typically cholestatic or mixed, onset ~2–12 weeks after starting) have been reported with ashwagandha products. Avoid in known liver disease; stop if jaundice or pruritus develops.

source.reference: LiverTox: Ashwagandha (NBK548536)

rasaushadhi.text: Contains mineral/metal ingredients (Rasaushadhi / bhasma). Heavy-metal content has been documented in about one fifth of Ayurvedic products sold online (Saper et al., JAMA 2008). Use only products with verified GMP and heavy-metal testing; specialist review is required, particularly in pregnancy, breastfeeding, children and renal impairment.

source.reference: Saper RB et al. Lead, mercury, and arsenic in US- and Indian-manufactured Ayurvedic medicines sold via the Internet. JAMA 2008;300(8):915-923
